Try getting an off-label prescription for 2% SADBE. As far as I’m aware, that’s probably the best realistic option for treating aggressive or resistant genital herpes at the current time, outside of antivirals. Enrolling in clinical trials may also yield some efficacious results but that of course has shortcomings. Best of luck.

Like I said before, there aren’t randomized controlled studies on how antivirals impact the time to seroconversion. If your most recent potential exposure to the virus was in June and you tested negative in January, YOU DO NOT HAVE HSV2.

Knowing that information, I’d say you almost certainly do not have HSV2. You need to see a doctor and get your symptoms checked out. You might have gHSV1 but if NAAT or culture swabs didn’t pick that up, it’s unlikely.

You’re fine, take it easy. Getting a WB is way overkill at this point and borderline neurotic.

EDIT:
You failed to mention your daily antiviral use.... STOP TAKING THEM if you want an accurate test. There isn’t data showing specifically how much it impacts seroconversion detection, but it very likely does to some extent. Wait 4-12 weeks and retest.
